messages:
sam: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-inc) opened a ticket: after enabling an int8 quant profile their embedding outputs changed from 1536 dims to 768 and similarity accuracy dropped. Happens consistently. Repro steps below.

jules: can you paste the exact API call and the model name/version + quant_profile used?

sam: sure — curl we used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large-v1","input":["doc1","doc2"],"params":{"precision":"int8-fast","batching":true,"batch_size":32}}'
```
Response shows embedding array length = 768. Customer says previous non-quantized run returned 1536.

devon: quick sanity: int8 quantization itself shouldn't change vector dimensionality unless you're switching to a different model variant. Are you sure model name/version is identical? sometimes we route to a compact variant.

sam: they passed model exactly as above. We checked request logs; model_version field is omitted so default routing applied.

hema: from quick look at logs — the quant_profile tag "int8-fast" maps to a profile that also enables our experimental "compact_head" optimization for that model family. That optimization reduces the projection head to 768 to save memory. It was supposed to be opt-in but the profile alias was mis-mapped.

jules: can you paste the raw response? sample snippet?

sam: snippet from response payload:
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, -0.234, ... /* total 768 floats */], "model":"redwood-embed-large-v1","metadata":{"quant_profile":"int8-fast"}}]}
```

devon: thanks. Also note batching=32 may mask the routing behavior — our smart routing can route smaller batches to a compact variant when under certain load profiles. That logic combines quant_profile + batch size to pick cost-optimized variant.

jules: ok that explains dimension change. What about quality drop?

hema: compact_head reduces output dim and was trained with a lightweight projection which degrades some semantics on this workload. We're seeing a measurable drop on their eval set. Repro steps to validate:
- run non-quant baseline with explicit model_version (v1.2.3) and no quant_profile
- run quant_profile=int8-fast with same model_version -> compare cos sims

sam: I ran both. Baseline (no quant) mean cosine to gold: 0.82. With int8-fast: 0.61.

l2-support: created ticket INC-4921 and flagged for priority escalation. ops-bot:link(https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4921) :white_check_mark:

devon: short-term mitigation for customer: force explicit model_version that maps to preserved-dim variant or set quant_profile to one of the profiles that preserve projection head, e.g. "preserve-dim-int8". Also set batching to 1 while we triage.

sam: confirmed forcing "model_version":"v1.2.3" and "params":{"precision":"int8-fast","force_preserve_dim":true} returns 1536 dims and restores quality to ~0.80. Good find.

jules: thanks — action items:
- hema to fix mapping for "int8-fast" so it doesn't implicitly enable compact_head unless explicitly requested (PR + rollout).
- devex to add docs note about quant_profile aliases and dimension side-effects.
- support to reach out to customer with workaround and update ticket.

hema: I'll open PR to remap profiles and add a regression test asserting embedding dims stable for preserved profiles.

sam: customer updated satisfied with workaround. will keep ticket open until fix shipped.

l2-support: marking follow-up tasks: add SDK warning when compress/compact profiles are used, and surface embedding dimension in API response header so customers can see if projection was changed.

devon: +1 on header, would help debugging.

sam: final note: root cause = profile alias mis-mapping + routing heuristic that prefers compact variant under certain batch/load combos. Resolved with explicit model_version or preserved-dim profile. Will coordinate on doc and PRs. :thumbsup:
